script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for May 18. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.
Dinosaurs didn't go extinct 66 million years ago.  One lineage survived, evolved, and thrived.  You see them every day—pecking at seeds, flying overhead, singing in trees.

Fossils from China show dinosaurs covered in feathers—not for flight, but perhaps for warmth or display. Feathers evolved before flight. T. rex may have had feathers as a juvenile. The scaly dinosaurs of movies are partly fiction. The closest living relatives of Tyrannosaurus rex are chickens and ostriches.  Protein analysis from T.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: Endings can be transformations.  What seems to disappear may simply change form.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Dinosaur Spotting - See the Living Past.

Here's your activity: Watch a bird today—any bird. Notice its movements, its body, its feathers. You're looking at a dinosaur—a direct descendant of creatures that walked with T. rex. 66 million years of evolution, still alive and flying around you. This helps you see birds as living dinosaurs.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about birds are dinosaurs can be applied to dinosaur spotting - see the living past. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
